We need to determine number of methyl groups in the sample's molecule. We have no description of molecule. We can get NMR spectra to infer. Use proton NMR to see methyl signals (singlet ~0.9 ppm). Could also use carbon NMR for methyl carbons (~10-30 ppm). We need to measure spectra. Use proton_nmr_spectra tool (expensive). Maybe carbon NMR cheaper? Both cost. But we need count methyl groups. Could use carbon NMR to count distinct methyl carbon signals. However overlapping may be ambiguous. Probably easiest: get proton NMR and count distinct methyl peaks (integrations). But we don't have integration values. The tool returns spectra as string maybe includes peaks with integration? Not sure.

We could also use HSQC to correlate. But that's more expensive.

Probably just get proton NMR. Let's call proton_nmr_spectra.
